analysis.title: Wind of change (Inflation-Linked Weekly, 2 September 2022)
key_insights: Eurozone August preliminary HICP printed at 9.1% headline and 4.3% core, in line with CA-CIB's forecast. Core has risen about 30bp every month since January, except June 2022 (stagnation near 3.75% after German public transport prices were cut).

CA-CIB's inner-core HICP measure (about 75% of the core basket) rose steadily from 2.55% YoY in January to 4.6% in July, and is estimated near 4.9% in August. Monthly acceleration has stayed between 25bp and 45bp over six months.

CA-CIB expects core inflation to keep rising in H222, driven by the end of Germany's 9-euro-ticket, more pass-through of energy prices into core HICP, and another wave of wage increases in Q422 and Q123.

CA-CIB's core HICP profile peaks slightly above 4.5% in September and Q422, then plateaus near 4.2% in H123. Average core is about 3.8% in both 2022 and 2023, 100bp above the ECB's June forecast for 2023.

Eurozone breakevens fell sharply last week (10Y down about 20bp, 2Y down about 100bp), attributed to the collapse in natural gas prices and high market expectations for the 9 September EC energy meeting.

CA-CIB thinks the market expects too much from the 9 September EC meeting, because a European electricity market reform is very complex and unlikely to be implemented quickly. Conviction is stated as low. Base case is more country-level measures rather than an EU-wide reform.

CA-CIB sees the second half of September as a possible window for a tactical long in EUR breakevens (10Y is the liquid point), after the ECB meeting, the EC meeting and French linker supply. Supports cited: strong linker index extension (about +0.28Y) and a strong end-month core inflation print.

The 1Y EUR inflation swap fell 80bp roll-adjusted (145bp unadjusted) between 17 August and 2 September. The 1Y1Y forward fell from 2.35% to 2.05%, the 2Y2Y lost about 10bp, and the 5Y5Y and longer forwards gained about 5bp.
CA-CIB has ex-tobacco HICP near 7% at the June 2023 horizon, 80bp above what the market prices (1Y inflation swap at 6.2%).

Government support measures (VAT cuts, discounted public transport, fuel rebates) are expected to end once energy prices ease, which could keep Eurozone inflation above 2% into mid-2024. This is what the 1Y1Y forward prices.

German energy assumptions: the October natural gas levy (+EUR0.24 per kWh) adds about 15% MoM to natural gas HICP, partly offset by an expected 7% VAT cut. Natural gas HICP is forecast at 88% YoY and electricity at 46% YoY at year-end.

Spain's 15% VAT cut on natural gas (21% to 6%) would take about 22bp off Spanish HICP and about 2.5bp off Eurozone HICP. Spanish public transport discounts would take about 30bp off Spanish core HICP.
Expected next-month events: an ECB hike with 75bp now the likely base case, linker supply returning (Germany, France, Italy), and EUR17.7bn of BTPei Sep-23 leaving the 1Y+ indices at end-September.
CA-CIB has no open trades. The last long inflation trade (1Y inflation swap) was closed in June. H122 P&L was 165bp across 11 trades with an 82% hit ratio.

US August CPI (due 13 September): CA-CIB expects headline at 8.1% YoY (40bp below July) and core at 6.0-6.1% YoY (about 15bp above July), driven by housing (OER 0.58% MoM, rents 0.67% MoM). The Bloomberg consensus was not yet formed.
Core CPI near 6% is described as much more than the Fed can tolerate. The expected declines in energy and core inflation after August are seen as encouraging for risk sentiment.

US component forecasts: services CPI up from 5.5% to 5.8% YoY, core goods down from 7.0% to 6.85% (peak 12.3% in February), food up from 10.9% to 11.5%, energy down from 33% to 24% with motor fuels falling from 44.9% to 27.7% YoY (-11% MoM in August).
Core goods inflation is expected to turn negative YoY at some point next year, mainly through negative used-car base effects.

trade_ideas.description: Tactical long in 10Y EUR breakevens in the second half of September. This is a potential window, not an open recommendation.
trade_ideas.rationale: After the ECB meeting, EC meeting and French linker supply, CA-CIB expects strong linker index extension and a strong end-month core inflation number.
trade_ideas.risk: Falling natural gas or crude oil prices. CA-CIB says there is no point going long inflation if energy prices are suffering.

risk_factors: Falling natural gas or crude oil prices would hurt long inflation positions.
Returning linker supply (Germany, France, Italy) is negative for breakevens.
The 9 September EC meeting could produce surprises, such as a gas price cap, and market expectations may be too high.
Uncertainty over the regulatory outlook for natural gas and electricity in Europe persists after the 9 September meeting.
Less favourable base effects into Q422 as the MoM moves of October to December 2021 roll out of the YoY calculation.
Government support measures may end once energy prices ease, which would push inflation higher.
US core CPI near 6% is above what the Fed can tolerate.
charts_described: Fig 1 plots Eurozone inner-core inflation reaching 4.59% YoY against core ex-food and energy.
Fig 5 shows EUR inflation swap forwards changes since 17 August: 1Y down 80bp roll-adjusted, 1Y1Y down 30bp, 2Y2Y down about 10bp, 5Y5Y up about 5bp.
vol_and_positioning: Dutch TTF natural gas rose about 80% in August before returning close to its starting point, causing large moves in inflation swaps and breakevens in thin August liquidity.
The EUR 1Y inflation swap rolled 65bp on 1 September (the 1Y reference point moved from May 2023 to June 2023), against CA-CIB's estimate of 60bp.
European equities fell almost 10% from mid-August (about 10% over two weeks), alongside hawkish central bank speeches at Jackson Hole. CA-CIB expects equities to do better than that.
Linker supply is returning (Germany, then France, then Italy), which is negative for breakevens all else equal.
A strong end-September index extension is expected (+0.28Y, matching September 2020) as EUR17.7bn of BTPei Sep-23 leaves the 1Y+ indices.
geopolitical: The European energy crisis and the emergency EC meeting of energy ministers on 9 September, hosted under the Czech EU presidency, on electricity market reform.
Reform options discussed: decoupling gas from electricity prices, capping the gas price as in Iberia, and pricing electricity at average production cost.
French PM Elisabeth Borne warned of energy rationing risk this winter. France has pledged EUR45bn of support, versus Germany at EUR60bn, Italy at EUR50bn and EUR236bn across the EU-27 (Bruegel).
Spain announced a 15% VAT cut on natural gas, from 21% to 6%, and reduced public transport prices from 1 September to year-end.

tension_points.bull_case: The market priced lower electricity and gas prices from an EC reform, and gas prices have collapsed. CA-CIB sees a tactical rebound in 10Y breakevens in late September on strong index extension and a strong core print.
tension_points.bear_case: CA-CIB thinks the market expects too much from the 9 September meeting, since reform is complex and slow. Returning linker supply is negative for breakevens.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Falling natural gas or crude oil prices would undermine a long breakeven trade.

theme_stances.key_argument: Core inflation is driven by past energy price increases and wages, and should keep accelerating through Q422.
theme_stances.evidence: our inner-core HICP measure has been steadily increasing since the start of the year

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is placing too much hope on the 9 September meeting because reform is complex and slow.
theme_stances.evidence: the market is placing too much hope on this meeting
